title: Layered configuration: INI, environment, and command-line options
sources: Python 3.14 Standard Library: configparser, argparse, os.environ; reviewed 2026-10-03
masterChecklist: Configuration management: environment variables, argparse, configparser, secrets boundaries
whyItMatters: The same program may run with different output formats or batch sizes on a laptop and a build server. Keeping those settings outside business logic avoids repeated code, while separating secrets from ordinary settings reduces accidental disclosure.
simpleExplanation: configparser reads INI-like sections and keys, returning text unless you request a typed conversion such as getint. argparse converts command-line options and validates declared choices. os.environ exposes the current process's environment settings. A team must choose and document precedence; this lesson uses command line first, then environment, then file defaults. A secret should be supplied through protected runtime configuration, not checked into an INI file or printed in logs. Even an environment variable is not magically safe: access and logging rules still matter.
mentalModel: An INI file is the default recipe, the environment is a kitchen-specific note, and a command-line flag is the instruction for this one run. A secret is a locked ingredient, not something to put on the public recipe card.
outcomes: Read a typed integer from an INI-style section.
Choose and test a clear precedence rule.
Use argparse choices for an explicit command-line contract.
Keep secret values out of examples, files, and output.

realWorldExample.scenario: A report service defaults to text output but CI requests JSON for one run.
realWorldExample.riskWithoutSetup: Unclear precedence makes behavior surprising; treating a config value as already typed can cause wrong arithmetic; logging an API token exposes credentials.
realWorldExample.professionalApproach: Define and test precedence, convert and validate values once at startup, pass a plain settings object to the report logic, and avoid printing or committing secrets.

workedExample.code:
import argparse
import configparser

config = configparser.ConfigParser()
config.read_string('[report]\nformat = text\nbatch_size = 4\n')
parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument('--format', choices=['text', 'json'])
args = parser.parse_args(['--format', 'json'])
fictional_environment = {'LEARNVERSE_REPORT_FORMAT': 'text', 'LEARNVERSE_API_TOKEN': 'demo-only'}
chosen = args.format or fictional_environment.get('LEARNVERSE_REPORT_FORMAT') or config['report']['format']
if chosen not in {'text', 'json'}:
    raise ValueError('unsupported format')
batch_size = config.getint('report', 'batch_size')
if batch_size < 1:
    raise ValueError('batch_size must be positive')
print(chosen)
print(batch_size)
print(bool(fictional_environment.get('LEARNVERSE_API_TOKEN')))
explanation: read_string loads a local sample INI section; no file or network is needed.
parse_args receives a fixed list so the example is deterministic. In a real CLI, parse_args() without a list reads the process command line.
The CLI's json value wins over the fictional environment's text value and the file's text default.
getint converts the INI value to an integer; the positive check rejects unusable batch sizes.
The final line prints only whether a fictional token exists, never its value. A real process would read an approved secret source at startup.
workedExample.safeExperiment: Change the fixed argument list to [] and observe the environment value win. Remove the environment format to observe the file default. Do not insert a real token.

procedure: Decide which settings are ordinary and which are secrets.
Document the order of precedence, such as CLI > environment > file default.
Parse and convert at the outer boundary, then validate allowed values and ranges.
Pass a validated settings value into the program's functions rather than reading globals everywhere.
Keep secret values out of source, command history, error messages, and logs; rotate any exposed credential.

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming every INI value already has the correct Python type.
commonMistakes.why: configparser stores values as strings unless a typed getter is used.
commonMistakes.avoid: Use getint/getboolean or an explicit conversion, then validate ranges.

commonMistakes.mistake: Expecting argparse choices to validate an environment value.
commonMistakes.why: argparse only checks the CLI value it parses.
commonMistakes.avoid: Validate the final resolved value after all precedence layers.

commonMistakes.mistake: Printing a token while diagnosing configuration.
commonMistakes.why: Logs may be retained or shared beyond the intended audience.
commonMistakes.avoid: Report presence or a redacted identifier, never the secret itself.

lab.title: Resolve a safe report format
lab.safety: Uses fictional in-memory settings; never stores or prints a real credential.
lab.starterCode:
import argparse
import configparser

config = configparser.ConfigParser()
config.read_string('[report]\nformat = text\nlimit = 3\n')
parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument('--format', choices=['text', 'json'])
args = parser.parse_args([])
environment = {'LEARNVERSE_REPORT_FORMAT': 'json'}
# Resolve CLI > environment > file, then print format and integer limit.
guidedSteps: Read the file default from the report section.
Choose args.format if supplied, otherwise the environment value, otherwise the file value.
Validate the final format against text/json because an environment value bypasses argparse choices.
Read limit with config.getint and print the selected format and limit.
checks: Output is json then 3 on separate lines.
The environment wins when no CLI flag is given.
An unsupported environment format raises a clear error after resolution.
hints: if chosen not in {'text', 'json'}: raise ValueError('unsupported format')
lab.solution:
import argparse
import configparser

config = configparser.ConfigParser()
config.read_string('[report]\nformat = text\nlimit = 3\n')
parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument('--format', choices=['text', 'json'])
args = parser.parse_args([])
environment = {'LEARNVERSE_REPORT_FORMAT': 'json'}
chosen = args.format or environment.get('LEARNVERSE_REPORT_FORMAT') or config['report']['format']
if chosen not in {'text', 'json'}:
    raise ValueError('unsupported format')
print(chosen)
print(config.getint('report', 'limit'))
lab.solutionExplanation: With no CLI flag, the environment's json overrides the file's text. getint returns an integer rather than a string.
challenges: Predict the output if --format text is added to the fixed argument list.
Find the bug: assuming argparse rejects an invalid value supplied only through environment.
Experiment: set the environment format to csv and confirm the deliberate error.

projectConnection.milestone: Add one settings resolver with documented precedence and a separate protected secret boundary.
projectConnection.definitionOfDone: Tests cover CLI/environment/file precedence, invalid values, typed conversion, and the fact that logs never expose a token.

assessment.question: Which setting wins in this lesson: CLI or environment?
assessment.answer: The CLI value wins when present.
assessment.explanation: The documented precedence is CLI, then environment, then file.

assessment.question: Why use config.getint for batch_size?
assessment.answer: INI values are stored as text; getint converts the value to an integer.
assessment.explanation: A range check is still needed afterward.

assessment.question: Does argparse choices validate a format read from environment?
assessment.answer: No. Validate the final resolved setting separately.
assessment.explanation: argparse only parses and checks its own input.
